summary: This note is a psychology research article (Trip et al., Frontiers in Psychology, 2019) investigating whether irrational beliefs and personality traits act as psychological mechanisms that make adolescents vulnerable to an extremist mind-set. It reviews models of radicalization and extremism (Stankov's tripartite militant extremist mind-set, Doosje's radical belief system, Ellis's rational emotive theory of irrational beliefs) and reports a study of 295 Romanian adolescents in Bihor County using the Militant Extremist Mind-Set Scale, CASI and Mini-IPIP. The article reports that confirmatory and structural models support the three-factor extremist mind-set, that global self-evaluation is the only irrational belief somewhat related to it, that neuroticism had no direct or indirect influence, and that religious adherence predicts extremist ideology. The excerpt is cut off in the Results section.
one_line: Study of 295 Romanian adolescents testing whether irrational beliefs and personality traits predict an extremist mind-set.
key_facts: The study sample consisted of 295 Romanian adolescents aged 15–18 years, with a mean age of 16.41.
The participants were recruited from several schools in Bihor County, located in the western part of Romania.
The tripartite militant extremist mind-set model proposed by Stankov et al. (2010b) includes War, God and West components.
McCauley and Moskalenko (2008, p. 416) define functional political radicalization as 'increased preparation for and commitment to intergroup conflict.'
Ellis (2003, p. 183) defined discomfort anxiety as emotional tension resulting when people feel their comfort or life is threatened and that they must get what they want.
The fifth structural model had adequate fit with RMSEA 0.054, CFI 0.958 and SRMS 0.047.
Global evaluation of self was the only irrational belief found to be somewhat related with the extremist mind-set, being part of it.
Neuroticism was not identified as having a direct influence on extremist mind-set, or an indirect influence through personality.
Religious adherence is described in the abstract as a good predictor of extremist ideology.
A global personality factor of low Intellect/Imagination, low Extraversion and high Agreeableness was described as a vulnerability factor for extremist ideology.
Questionnaires were administered in paper-pencil format to 400 students between October 2017 and March 2018, and 295 (73.75%) were used.
The Militant Extremist Mind-Set Scale had Cronbach's alphas of 0.81 (War), 0.86 (God) and 0.80 (West) in this study.
The Mini-IPIP was developed by Donnellan et al. (2006) and contains 20 items, four per Big Five factor.
Using Mahalanobis distance, the authors identified and removed 38 univariate or multivariate outliers, leaving a final sample of 257 in the CFA.
Sample composition: 176 Romanians (59.7%), 70 Hungarians (23.7%), 49 Roma (16.6%); 172 Orthodox Christian (58.3%).
